parts.text: Tμν tells us how the matter action changes when we deform the spacetime metric.
A Killing vector represents a direction in which the spacetime geometry has a symmetry.
For example, if the metric doesn't change under time translations,
then ϵμ=(1,0,0,0) is a Killing vector.
Then there is a conserved energy.
If the spacetime is symmetric under spatial translations, there is conserved momentum.
If it is symmetric under rotations, there is conserved angular momentum.
This is the clean infinitesimal version.
Now the crucial thing is: σ(x) is arbitrary.
That means I can choose the Weyl rescaling independently at different points.
Tμμ​ measures the response to local scaling of the metric.​ Therefore scale/Weyl invariance corresponds to zero trace.
But after quantization, sometimes the symmetry of the classical action does not survive exactly.
The nonzero quantum trace is related to the central charge c.
